architectural-decision-records.why: records the enforcement-nudge decision and its honest ceiling
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR 0066: an always-on enforcement nudge (sibling of the sync nudge) for advisory consumers, cleared by intent+confirm; esk-genesis scaffolds the ruleset + travels apply-ruleset.sh; the admin-only-setting ceiling stated
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

pattern-selector.why: chose the nudge design against the forces, naming the rejected alternatives
pattern-selector.what: selected the always-on nudge (reusing the sync-nudge shape) over a live GitHub API check (needs admin token, breaks on forks, rejected by the repo for itself) and over a committed-file-only check; recorded in the ADR
quotes: A pattern removes one specific kind of failure or rot

verifiable-quality-gates.why: every new behavior has a discriminating test proven to detect
verifiable-quality-gates.what: pure tests for decideEnforcementNudge (fires advisory, clears only on ruleset+applied, caps then quiets, intent-not-enough) and rulesetRequires; emitter integration tests that the nudge is prepended, clears, is origin-silent, and subagent-silent
quotes: replace each check with a no-op and require its test to fail

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: tested at unit level and end-to-end through the emitter in a fake consumer
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: unit tests on the pure decision; integration tests run the real emitter in a throwaway consumer repo with the actual signal files (workflow, ruleset, marker) and assert the injected context
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: coupling fires on the emitter/installer change; behaviors pinned as executable scenarios
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: the behaviors (advisory consumer nudged, enforced cleared, committed-but-not-applied still nudged, non-consumer silent, subagent silent) are written as discriminating tests at the lowest layer that proves them
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment. Every time this

judge-arch.why: reviewed the change in fresh context before the PR
judge-arch.what: ran judge-arch on the nudge, the emitter wiring, the genesis ruleset/apply-script scaffolding, and apply-ruleset.sh; recorded in the arch-review log
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion

skeptical-audit.why: each claim carries evidence; the honest ceiling is stated, not hidden
skeptical-audit.what: proved the nudge fires/clears end-to-end through the real emitter in a fake consumer, and stated plainly that intent+confirm proves committed+applied, not live GitHub enforcement (admin-only, out of scope)
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, or feature flag; this is CI-governance (branch protection) tooling, not a release mechanism

sre-operational-readiness.why: no runtime service, SLI/SLO, or production alerting; this nudges a dev session, not a running system

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: no auth/input/crypto/session/file surface; the nudge reads local files with no shell

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal data, retention, or schema/data migration

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no product system/data architecture change; always-on emitter + installer

arch-encode.why: no caught mistake encoded into a new rule in this change

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no user-facing UI; emitter, installer, scripts, tests

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no user-facing UI or workflow for people
